method: Original summaries checked against primary publisher, author and source-text evidence. Exact captured ISBN, title, author and language binding. Where the source is a different printing, only the work premise is used. No private GSC data or copied blurbs.

entries.title: The Mirror of Infinite Endings
entries.author: Stephanie Garber
entries.text: Jacks and Evangeline have found happiness in the Hollow, but a secret still has the power to change their story. Stephanie Garber returns to these characters in an illustrated companion novella to Once Upon a Broken Heart. The focus is on what follows their earlier adventures and on a hidden truth that could reshape the past. Written for readers familiar with the trilogy, the book revisits its romantic fairy-tale world, with illustrations by Lotusbubble.
entries.identityNotes: Exact ISBN verified at publisher. Companion novella published September 2026, distinct from the three main novels. Illustrator confirmed.

entries.title: A Curse for True Love
entries.author: Stephanie Garber
entries.text: Evangeline Fox appears to have the fairy-tale life she wanted: a prince, a castle and a future in the Magnificent North. Yet missing memories conceal the cost of that happiness, and her husband has reasons to keep the truth from her. Jacks remains bound up in the story she cannot fully remember. The third main novel in Once Upon a Broken Heart brings Stephanie Garber's trilogy to its conclusion through conflicting loyalties, dangerous bargains and the question of whom Evangeline can trust.
entries.identityNotes: Exact ISBN verified. Main trilogy conclusion, not the later illustrated companion. Opening situation only; no resolution disclosed.

entries.title: Reckless
entries.author: Lauren Roberts
entries.text: Paedyn Gray is on the run after the Purging Trials, and Kai has been ordered to bring her back. As the king's Enforcer, his duty conflicts with his feelings for the woman he is hunting. Their pursuit leads beyond Ilya into a desert and a city where power works differently. Reckless continues Lauren Roberts's Powerless trilogy as its second novel, following the consequences of the first book through an uneasy mixture of attraction, survival and allegiance.
entries.identityNotes: Exact UK ISBN verified. Second main Powerless novel; premise avoids revealing the outcome of the pursuit.

entries.title: Fearless
entries.author: Lauren Roberts
entries.text: Paedyn and Kai return to Ilya facing a choice that could alter their lives and the kingdom around them. Their relationship has become entangled with royal demands, and wanting a future together does not make their competing obligations disappear. Fearless is the third and concluding novel in Lauren Roberts's Powerless trilogy. It follows the consequences of Powerless and Reckless, bringing the central conflict between love, loyalty and political power toward its resolution.
entries.identityNotes: Exact ISBN and trilogy conclusion verified. No ending or plot twist disclosed.

entries.title: Inheritance
entries.author: Christopher Paolini
entries.text: Eragon and his dragon Saphira prepare to confront Galbatorix after a long struggle that has tested their abilities and cost their allies dearly. Training and earlier victories have brought them this far, but defeating the king demands more than confidence in their growing strength. Inheritance is the fourth novel in Christopher Paolini's original Inheritance Cycle. It concludes that sequence's central conflict in Alagaësia, continuing the story established in Eragon, Eldest and Brisingr.
entries.identityNotes: Author identifies Book Four and original cycle conclusion. Work-level premise only; no bonus content from newer editions attributed to the captured Corgi ISBN.

entries.title: Crossroads of Twilight (The Wheel of Time, Number 10)
entries.author: Robert Jordan
entries.text: Mat tries to escape Ebou Dar with the Daughter of the Nine Moons, while Perrin faces difficult choices in his effort to rescue Faile from the Shaido. Elsewhere, the cleansing of saidin has changed the situation around Rand without removing the danger posed by uncertain allies. Crossroads of Twilight is the tenth main Wheel of Time novel. Robert Jordan follows several connected journeys as the characters respond to upheaval and prepare for conflicts still ahead.
entries.identityNotes: Publisher supports tenth-volume position and work premise. Selected older ISBN captured independently; no features of the cited later printing claimed.

entries.title: Lord of Chaos (The Wheel of Time, Book 6)
entries.author: Robert Jordan
entries.text: Rand al'Thor seeks men who can channel as he tries to strengthen his position against the Shadow. The divided Aes Sedai also have plans for the Dragon Reborn, and apparent offers of help carry competing political interests. In the sixth main Wheel of Time novel, Robert Jordan develops the struggle over who can guide or control Rand's growing power. Lord of Chaos continues the series through uneasy alliances, new institutions and mistrust between people who claim to share an enemy.
entries.identityNotes: Publisher verifies sixth-volume position and premise. No ending or later-edition material included.

entries.title: Going postal
entries.author: Terry Pratchett
entries.text: Condemned conman Moist von Lipwig is offered a chance to survive by taking charge of Ankh-Morpork's neglected post office. Restoring the mail service means dealing with undelivered letters, unusual staff and powerful competition from a newer communications network. His talent for persuasion may be useful, but the job requires him to take responsibility for something beyond his own escape. Going Postal introduces Moist as a leading character within Terry Pratchett's Discworld, combining a public-service revival with comic intrigue.
entries.identityNotes: Official author/publisher catalogue verifies premise and Moist entry point. No printing-specific features asserted.

entries.title: Captains Courageous (Lake Illustrated Classics, Collection 3)
entries.author: Rudyard Kipling
entries.text: Harvey Cheyne, a wealthy and demanding boy, falls overboard and is rescued by fishermen working the Grand Banks. Unable to buy an immediate return home, he must live and work alongside the crew, learning practical skills and respect for people whose lives differ from his own. This Lake Illustrated Classics edition presents Kipling's sea adventure in an illustrated series. At its centre is Harvey's changing understanding of responsibility, friendship and the work that keeps a fishing vessel going.
entries.identityNotes: Original public-domain story checked for premise. Captured edition title identifies Lake Illustrated Classics; no claim of unabridged text, page count or an illustrator from another adaptation.

entries.title: Kim
entries.author: Rudyard Kipling
entries.text: Kim, an orphan growing up in India, travels with a Tibetan lama searching for a sacred river. His knowledge of local life also draws him into the intelligence rivalry known as the Great Game. The journeys connect a spiritual search with espionage, placing different kinds of loyalty in tension. Rudyard Kipling's novel follows Kim through the cultures and political relationships of nineteenth-century British India, asking where he belongs as others recognise and try to use his abilities.
entries.identityNotes: Publisher verifies work premise and historical setting. No physical features or supplementary material from the newer cited edition included.

entries.title: Edge Of Eternity
entries.author: Ken Follett
entries.text: Five interconnected families face the divisions of the Cold War as their lives move through political upheaval in the United States, Europe and the Soviet Union. The Berlin Wall and the American civil-rights struggle become part of personal stories shaped by relationships, ambition and competing beliefs. Edge of Eternity completes Ken Follett's Century trilogy, following later generations of the families introduced in its earlier volumes. It combines a broad historical canvas with the consequences of public events for individual lives.
entries.identityNotes: Publisher verifies Century trilogy finale and family/historical scope. Work premise only, without importing later-paperback features into selected Turtleback edition.

entries.title: Winter of the World
entries.author: Ken Follett
entries.text: Five families become caught in the rise of Nazism, the Second World War and the changes that follow it. Beginning in Berlin in 1933, the story follows a new generation whose choices connect Germany, Britain, the United States and the Soviet Union. Private loyalties are tested by political commitments and the demands of war. Winter of the World is the second volume of Ken Follett's Century trilogy, continuing the family histories begun in Fall of Giants.
entries.identityNotes: Author synopsis confirms second Century volume, 1933 opening and five families. No ending or edition extras asserted.

entries.title: Evening and the Morning
entries.author: Ken Follett
entries.text: In England in 997, a young boatbuilder's life is disrupted by a Viking raid, a Norman noblewoman enters an unfamiliar marriage, and a monk hopes to create a centre of learning. Their ambitions bring them into conflict with an unscrupulous bishop. Ken Follett connects these lives in a story of power, work and the effort to build something lasting. The Evening and the Morning is a prequel to The Pillars of the Earth, exploring the earlier world from which Kingsbridge develops.
entries.identityNotes: Author verifies 997 setting, three central strands and Kingsbridge prequel. Selected title lacks initial article; exact catalogue binding retained.

entries.title: Code Rebecca
entries.author: Ken Follett
entries.text: In Caïro probeert de Duitse spion Alex Wolff in 1942 militaire informatie door te geven aan Rommel. Hij gebruikt een code die verbonden is met de roman Rebecca. De Britse officier William Vandam probeert hem met hulp van Elene Fontana op te sporen, terwijl de oorlog in Noord-Afrika de inzet steeds groter maakt. Code Rebecca is de Nederlandse vertaling van The Key to Rebecca. Ken Follett verbindt de spionagejacht met misleiding, persoonlijke risico's en de strijd om betrouwbare informatie.
entries.identityNotes: Author synopsis verifies original work and premise. Dutch translation identity retained from selected catalogue; no features of a newer edition added.

entries.title: Het Modigliani-schandaal
entries.author: Ken Follett
entries.text: Kunsthistorica Dee Sleign hoort over een verdwenen schilderij van Modigliani en gaat op zoek. Zodra anderen lucht krijgen van de mogelijke vondst, verandert die zoektocht in een wedloop waarin kunsthandelaren en andere belanghebbenden hun eigen plannen volgen. Ken Follett laat zien hoe geld, reputatie en de belofte van een meesterwerk elkaar beïnvloeden. Het Modigliani-schandaal is de Nederlandse vertaling van zijn vroege misdaadroman The Modigliani Scandal, met de Europese kunstwereld als decor voor bedrog en rivaliteit.
entries.identityNotes: Author verifies original work, Dee Sleign and art-world premise. No unsupported details about selected Bruna printing.

entries.title: Figuranten
entries.author: Arnon Grunberg
entries.text: Elvira Lopez, Broccoli en Ewald Krieg dromen van een ander leven en van een toekomst in de filmwereld. Hun plan om door te breken krijgt de naam Operatie Brando, maar tussen de gewenste rollen en hun dagelijkse bestaan blijft een grote afstand. Arnon Grunberg volgt hun ambities met humor en aandacht voor de teleurstelling die daarachter schuilgaat. Figuranten is een roman over vriendschap, zelfbeelden en het verlangen om eindelijk iemand van betekenis te worden.
entries.identityNotes: Publisher verifies three central characters and Operatie Brando. Work-level description, no claims about current reprint design or extras.

entries.title: Het aapje dat geluk pakt
entries.author: Arnon Grunberg
entries.text: Jean Baptist Warnke werkt als diplomaat in Lima en heeft een vrouw en twee dochters. De ontmoeting met Malena brengt beweging in een bestaan dat op het eerste gezicht geregeld lijkt. Wanneer hij een belangrijke receptie mist, krijgen zijn persoonlijke keuzes ook gevolgen voor zijn werk. In deze novelle onderzoekt Arnon Grunberg hoe het verlangen naar geluk botst met verplichtingen en zelfbedrog. Het aapje dat geluk pakt volgt een man die de greep op zijn zorgvuldig ingerichte leven verliest.
entries.identityNotes: Publisher verifies Lima, family, Malena and missed reception. Described as a novella; no audiobook or current-reprint features imported.

entries.title: De overgave
entries.author: Arthur Japin
entries.text: In Texas wordt het gezin van Granny in 1836 getroffen door een aanval op het fort waar de familie woont. Er vallen doden en kinderen worden meegenomen. Terwijl zij probeert verder te leven, blijft de hoop op terugkeer verbonden met herinneringen aan geweld en verlies. Arthur Japin baseert De overgave op de geschiedenis van de familie Parker. De historische roman onderzoekt hoe wraak, vergeving en volharding naast elkaar kunnen bestaan wanneer een familie uit elkaar is geslagen.
entries.identityNotes: Author page explicitly lists selected hardcover ISBN 9789029565295. Historical novel based on Parker family; not presented as nonfiction.

entries.title: Play it as it lays
entries.author: Joan Didion
entries.text: Joan Didion places a woman's personal crisis against the unsettled social world of late-1960s America. Hollywood, Las Vegas and the Mojave Desert form the setting for a novel whose spare language brings emotional distance and disillusionment into focus. Play It as It Lays examines the gap between outward appearances and an inner life in distress. It is fiction rather than one of Didion's essay collections or memoirs, concentrating its view of a troubled society through one woman's experience.
entries.identityNotes: Publisher verifies novel form, setting and central focus. No David Thomson introduction claimed for selected 1970 edition.

entries.title: The Dip
entries.author: Seth Godin
entries.text: Seth Godin asks when a difficult stretch is worth working through and when it signals that effort would be better spent elsewhere. He distinguishes a temporary dip on the way to progress from a dead end that continued persistence will not solve. This short book applies that distinction to decisions about projects, work and ambition. The Dip presents quitting as a choice to examine deliberately, encouraging readers to judge where sustained effort has a useful purpose.
entries.identityNotes: Exact original ISBN verified. Author’s decision framework described without promising career or financial results.

entries.title: Linchpin
entries.author: Seth Godin
entries.text: Seth Godin argues that valuable work involves more than reliably following instructions. He encourages people to use judgement, make connections and bring creative initiative to situations that do not have a ready-made answer. Linchpin considers the fear and resistance that can keep workers from taking that responsibility. Through examples and arguments about modern employment, the book invites readers to examine how they contribute and what it means to become someone an organisation depends on.
entries.identityNotes: Publisher supports work-level argument. Selected original hardcover kept distinct from cited paperback; no later supplementary content or guaranteed outcomes.

entries.title: The Host
entries.author: Stephenie Meyer
entries.text: An alien called Wanderer is placed inside Melanie Stryder's body, expecting to take over a human host. Melanie's consciousness refuses to disappear, and her memories draw Wanderer toward the people she loves. Sharing one body forces the two into an uneasy relationship as they become involved with humans who have escaped the invasion. The Host combines science fiction and romance, using their conflict to explore identity, attachment and the possibility of sympathy between beings who begin as enemies.
entries.identityNotes: Author verifies Melanie/Wanderer premise. Standalone science-fiction romance context, without importing Twilight details or film material.

entries.title: The Short Second Life of Bree Tanner
entries.author: Stephenie Meyer
entries.text: Bree Tanner is a newly created vampire whose brief part in Eclipse leaves much of her experience outside Bella's view. This companion novella moves the focus to Bree and the dangerous world of newborn vampires around her. Stephenie Meyer follows the events from another perspective, allowing familiar conflicts to be seen through a character with different knowledge and loyalties. The Short Second Life of Bree Tanner supplements Eclipse, making it a companion for readers of that Twilight novel.
entries.identityNotes: Author announcement verifies novella, Bree viewpoint and Eclipse relationship. No invented plot resolution or additional edition features.

entries.title: These Violent Delights
entries.author: Chloe Gong
entries.sourceName: Margaret K. McElderry Books / Simon & Schuster
entries.text: In Shanghai in 1926, Juliette Cai and Roma Montagov belong to rival gangs and share a painful history. A deadly outbreak threatens both sides of the city, forcing them to investigate together despite their distrust. Chloe Gong reimagines Romeo and Juliet through a historical fantasy that combines a gang feud, an uneasy romantic connection and a supernatural threat. These Violent Delights begins a two-book story, with the struggle for the city testing loyalties that once seemed fixed.
entries.identityNotes: Exact ebook ISBN verified. Publisher explicitly Margaret K. McElderry Books: catalogue incorrectly contains author Chloe Gong as publisher; narrowly scoped display correction accompanies summary.

entries.title: Find Your Why
entries.author: Simon Sinek
entries.text: Simon Sinek, David Mead and Peter Docker offer exercises for identifying the purpose behind a person's work or a team's shared efforts. The guide develops the ideas introduced in Start with Why into a process of reflecting on experiences, noticing recurring themes and expressing a sense of purpose. Find Your Why is intended for both individuals and groups. Its emphasis is practical: helping participants examine what motivates their contribution and put that understanding into words they can use.
entries.identityNotes: Exact ISBN and coauthors verified. Practical companion to Start with Why; outcomes not guaranteed.

entries.title: Leaders Eat Last: Why Some Teams Pull Together and Others Don't
entries.author: Simon Sinek
entries.text: Simon Sinek examines how leaders can create conditions in which people trust one another and feel supported at work. He argues that responsibility for a team includes protecting its members and putting their wellbeing ahead of a leader's immediate advantage. Leaders Eat Last uses examples from organisations to consider cooperation, loyalty and the effects of a fearful workplace. The book presents Sinek's perspective on leadership and shared purpose, asking what helps a group act together over time.
entries.identityNotes: Author verifies leadership/trust scope. No later expanded-edition chapters included; biological or performance claims not repeated as established fact.

entries.title: I Want to Go Home!
entries.author: Gordon Korman
entries.text: Rudy Miller has no interest in enjoying summer camp. While the people around him expect activities, friendship and enthusiasm, he concentrates on finding a way to leave. His resistance turns the organised camp routine into a series of comic conflicts and escape attempts. Gordon Korman's I Want to Go Home! centres on a boy who refuses to accept the holiday planned for him, finding humour in the clash between his determination and the adults responsible for keeping him there.
entries.identityNotes: Author page verifies Rudy and camp-escape premise. Exaggerations in fictional home letter not asserted as events.

entries.title: Crown of Swords
entries.author: Robert Jordan
entries.text: Rand al'Thor prepares to move against Sammael in Illian while rebellion and unreliable allies threaten the authority he has gained. The men who can channel add another uncertain force to a world already divided over the Dragon Reborn. A Crown of Swords is the seventh main Wheel of Time novel, continuing Robert Jordan's interwoven struggles over power, trust and the war against the Shadow. It follows Lord of Chaos and assumes familiarity with the characters' earlier choices.
entries.identityNotes: Exact Tor ISBN verified, seventh-volume position. Catalogue title Crown of Swords retained for identity matching.

entries.title: Dragons at Crumbling Castle
entries.author: Terry Pratchett
entries.text: Dragons have appeared at Crumbling Castle, and young Ralph is sent to deal with them while King Arthur's knights are away. A knight and a wizard join his adventure, one of fourteen stories in this collection of Terry Pratchett's early writing for children. Other tales explore equally playful situations involving unexpected creatures and journeys. Dragons at Crumbling Castle is a collection of separate comic adventures, offering a different introduction to Pratchett's imagination from a full-length Discworld novel.
entries.identityNotes: Official catalogue verifies fourteen children’s stories and title-story premise. No illustration count or extras from another printing imported.

entries.title: A Column of Fire
entries.author: Ken Follett
entries.text: Ned Willard returns to Kingsbridge in 1558 to find personal relationships entangled with religious divisions. His work for Elizabeth I draws him into a struggle to protect her rule, as rival beliefs and political ambitions connect England with conflicts across Europe. Ken Follett combines espionage, romance and historical change in this Kingsbridge novel. A Column of Fire follows a later generation than The Pillars of the Earth and World Without End, moving the series into the sixteenth century.
entries.identityNotes: Author verifies 1558 opening, Ned and Elizabeth’s intelligence network. No ending or edition-specific extras.

entries.title: De mensendokter
entries.author: Arnon Grunberg
entries.text: Arnon Grunberg beantwoordt vragen van lezers over relaties, dagelijkse dilemma's en de betekenis die mensen aan hun leven proberen te geven. De antwoorden uit zijn rubriek in Vrij Nederland zijn samengebracht in deze bundel. Hij bekijkt de problemen met ironie en een literaire blik, waarbij een stellige oplossing vaak plaatsmaakt voor een onverwachte gedachte. De mensendokter laat zien hoe persoonlijk advies ook een manier kan zijn om menselijke verlangens, gewoonten en tegenstrijdigheden te onderzoeken.
entries.identityNotes: Publisher verifies collected Vrij Nederland advice columns. Literary collection, not a medical handbook; no health claims.

entries.title: Unteachables
entries.author: Gordon Korman
entries.text: The pupils in room 117 have been written off by their school, and their teacher, Zachary Kermit, is counting down to retirement. His own career was damaged by a cheating scandal years earlier, leaving him with little enthusiasm for another class. Yet this unlikely group begins to challenge what everyone expects of them. Gordon Korman's school comedy follows the changing relationship between overlooked students and a disillusioned teacher as they discover reasons to care about one another.
entries.identityNotes: Author verifies room 117, Kermit and school premise. No ending or unsupported edition features included.
